Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, attaching our MVP token profile and a short prompt set so your team can start sizing models. A few important notes up front:

- ~12% of requests will require a long-context retrieval (user history + doc snippets), pushing context to ~2,500–3,000 tokens.

Appreciate it —

Hi Anita / Sean —

Thanks for the prompt set and token CSV, Anita — good visibility. Quick answers:
- Long-context split: our read is ~70% external doc retrieval (chunked RAG) + 30% user-history-heavy sessions.
- Latency: for the pilot your stated product goal is 1s p50 on the main path and <1.5s p95 on long-context is acceptable. If you want stricter SLOs we can recommend Dedicated capacity.

Initial model shortlist for pilot (tradeoffs noted):
1) Llama-2-13B (HF-optimized) — strong instruction-following, good for retrieval-heavy RAG where hallucination control matters. Cost: medium.
2) Mixtral-8x7B (quantized q4) — efficient per-token, good throughput for high QPS peaks, slightly lower long-tail reasoning quality. Cost: low–medium.
3) Redwood-Chat-7B-lite (vetted, quantized) — lowest cost, good for short context and bursty low-latency calls; recommend as fallback for degraded capacity.

Sizing assumptions (pilot):
- Baseline volume: 8 QPS sustained ⇒ ~8 QPS * average 200 tokens/request * 3600s = ~5.76M tokens/hour.
- Peak window: 45 QPS for 30 minutes ⇒ ~45 * 250 * 1800s ≈ 20.25M tokens for the peak period (we plan for ~3x baseline headroom).
- Long-context requests (12%): these will drive larger cost per query; assume average 2,500 tokens per long call vs 200 for short calls.

Attachments you might expect from us during sizing: a cleaned hourly traffic CSV (we can produce), plus a handful of benchmark prompts per model.

Next steps: Ben will put together an hourly token envelope with preferred serving tier and caching/batching recommendations. We suggest a short 45-minute technical sync tomorrow to validate the model shortlist and test prompts.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

Anita / team —

Attached is a quick sizing snapshot and recommended request envelope (CSV + PNG). Highlights:
- Recommended pilot serving tier: Hosted API on a mixed-slate with autoscaling and prefix caching enabled. Move to Dedicated if you need p95 long-context <900ms consistently.
- Hourly envelope (conservative): 6M–8M tokens/hour baseline, with capacity reservations for up to 22M tokens during peak hours.
- Caching: enabling KV prefix caching for the top 30% of repeated prompts reduces tokens by ~18% on our sample.
- Batching strategy: small aggressive batching for mixtral-8x7B, prefer 8–12 token-aware batch size for Llama-2-13B to balance latency/cost.

Concrete asks from BrightWave for tomorrow's sync:
- A sample of 10 long-context queries (one per major flow) so we can run a quick latency/quality baseline.
- Confirm which elements of the history must be sent (full thread vs last 3 messages) — we recommended last 3 messages + doc excerpts.

Attachments included: BW_peak_hour_qps_snapshot.png (visual), BrightWave_sizing_snapshot.csv.

I'll be available for the 45-min sync window tomorrow 11:00–12:00 PDT. Please confirm a time.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
